doc.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1960-09-03

title: The Whitman Sisters and spiritualism
summary: Boote describes the Whitman Sisters' touring show and one sister who became a spiritualist in Chicago; Allen asks what that involves.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, they was one of the old show groups. You know, they had the minstrel shows and they had, they had traveled quite a lot over the United States with Whitman sisters. They had, I guess there was minstrels during that time, you know, when they traveled around. And of late, they all, when they went north, they were quite popular and now, it's about three left and one, she's a spiritualist and Alice and, I've forgotten all their names now, but they were quite well known all over the South here. How many were there? I think it was about four. Four.
Yeah, she's a spiritualist in Chicago now. Essie, Alice, and they would come back. But they, they traveled with their own, own band and everything.
Well, what does a spiritualist do?

Well, the spiritualist, they, they have a church, but they're like those mediums. They read, you know, they claim they can read and see the future and all like this. And they preach too. because a lot of theatrical people and smart people, some of them take, gets it as a racket and some may be sincere, I couldn't say, but it, it's nice money in it.
